newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trade slow, focus on techs.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index trade slow, focus on techs.

text.p: Activity in U.S. stock index options were generally slow, except for the bubbly technology sector, as the underlying market drifted in narrow ranges, traders said.

The market appeared to be awaiting a cue from the bond market, which was also tight-ranged as the Treasury's refunding auctions began today, said Jack Callahan, an independent market-maker for S&P 100 index options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE).
"They're watching the refunding, although there's no reason for anything to shake loose there," he said.

With one hour of trading left, the busiest OEX option was the August 950 calls, with only 4,281 contracts traded. On the put side, at-the-money August 930 and a few out-of-the-money puts had traded slightly more than 2,000 contracts each.
The OEX was up 3.59 points at 931.60 at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.
The CBOE volatility index, which reflects implied volatility levels for near-month OEX options, was off 0.43 point at 22.00.
"It's coming down to the lower end of what it has been," said Rod Jamieson, vice president of option strategies at EVEREN Securities.
The VIX has been ranging largely between 20 and 25 this year after trading mostly in the upper teens in 1996 and the mid-teens in 1995.
Callahan said the shrinkage in volatilities could be a sign that the market was going into a temporary lull after hectic business in the past few months.
But traders added the technology sector continued attracting a lot of investor interest.
Jamieson noted that there was a lot of call selling in individual tech stock options, despite the strength in the sector, perhaps due to position squaring and buy-writes.

A brokerage firm trader said a lot of speculative investors who had put on call positions ahead of the quarterly earnings reports were taking profits, if they had not already done so, as the earnings season had peaked out.
Among the few remaining big technology names yet to come out with earnings results, Cisco Systems Inc was due to release its earnings later in the day after the market closed today.
Cisco's August 80 calls traded more than 4,000 contracts, while the 80 puts traded about 3,500 contracts. Both were among the busiest options on CBOE.
Implied volatility for the August 80 strikes stood at around 50 percent, compared with the stock's one-month actual volatility of about 25 percent.
According to Zacks Investment Research, Wall Street analysts expected Cisco's earnings to come in at $0.55 per share, but traders said some unpublished forecasts had them at up to $0.60.
"It (Cisco stock's performance after earnings results) will be a barometer for the whole high-tech sector," said Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, a market-making firm at CBOE.
